financials_interim.notes: Q1 FY2026/27 (quarter ended 30.06.2026), same filing as GROUP row (p.3-4,6), COMPANY (parent, standalone holding-company) basis. Company has no trading revenue of its own (a pure holding company); operating_profit = -1,776 (admin expenses only, no revenue). PBT=-1,575 vs -606 in 30.06.2025; both periods are losses at the parent-only level, immaterial in scale, driven purely by holding-company overheads not offset by dividend income this quarter. EPS printed as -0.01 for the period (vs printed as nil for the 30.06.2025 quarter) -- ties: -1,575,000 / 189,689,990 shares = -0.0083, rounds to -0.01. total_liabilities = total_assets - total_equity = 2,830,680-2,826,464 = 4,216 ~= printed 4,215 (rounding). No inventory, no short/long-term borrowings at Company level (all blank/nil, none disclosed). shares_in_issue same combined 189,689,990 (dual-class) as Group -- Company EPS/NAPS both computed on this base per Note 4/5.

Q1 FY2026/27 (quarter ended 30.06.2026 = period ended, since this is the first quarter of the FYE-March fiscal year), p.3 income statement, p.4 balance sheet, p.6 cash flow. GROUP basis. operating_profit = 'Profit/(Loss) from Operations' (338,879) which already nets Other Operating Income (52,670); cost_of_sales/gross_profit are the filing's own lines. profit_before_tax bridge verified: 338,879 (operating) + 131,438 (net finance income) + 14,372 (FV gain on FVTPL investments) = 484,689 ~= 484,690 (printed PBT) -- ties. IMPORTANT extraction-order correction: the 'Fair Value Gain/(Loss) on Investments' row's raw PDF text extracts with the two years apparently reversed vs the header order; the correct assignment (14,372 for 30.06.2026, 306,291 for 30.06.2025) was confirmed via this PBT bridge and via the cash flow statement's adjustment line 'Fair Value Gain from Investment - Measured at FVTPL (14,372) (306,291)', both of which corroborate 14,372=2026, 306,291=2025 -- the value used here. Tax expense 2026=77,655; the 30.06.2025 comparator column shows nil tax (blank), i.e. PAT2025=PBT2025 exactly (426,681=426,681), consistent with zero tax that quarter. Similarly, two balance-sheet SUBTOTAL rows ('Total Non-Current Assets' and 'Total Current Liabilities') print their two date-columns in reversed order relative to the header and relative to their own component lines above them (verified by summing each subtotal's component lines, which sum correctly to the OTHER printed number, not the one aligned under the 30.06.2026 header) -- this does not affect any field stored here since current_assets (16,319,020, unreversed, verified against Operational Review text on p.2 which states 'Total Current Assets were Rs. 16,319Mn ... as at 30th June 2026') and current_liabilities were cross-checked by re-summing their own unambiguous component lines: current_liabilities (30.06.2026) = Trade & Other Payables 1,111,684 + Interest Bearing Borrowings Due Within One Year 3,582,684 + Current Lease 33,219 + Income Tax Payable 77,792 + Bank Overdraft 189,449 = 4,994,828 ~= 4,994,827 (the SECOND, not first, printed number on that garbled subtotal row). Total Liabilities (6,965,327) and Total Assets (28,645,343) rows themselves are NOT reversed and tie exactly: 1,970,499 (non-current liab, unreversed) + 4,994,827 (current liab, corrected) = 6,965,326 ~= 6,965,327; 6,965,327 + 21,680,016 (total equity) = 28,645,343 = total assets. Total equity (21,680,016) includes NCI (11,707,337); owners' equity alone is 9,972,679, matching Operational Review's 'Rs.9,973Mn'. short_term_borrowings = Interest Bearing Borrowings Due Within One Year (3,582,684) + Bank Overdraft (189,449) = 3,772,133 (no single dedicated 'short-term borrowings' line exists separate from these two, so both are combined as short-term debt, consistent with the KVAL precedent in this DB). long_term_borrowings = Interest Bearing Borrowings Due After One Year (38,888) only; the non-current lease obligation (202,262) is excluded as it is a lease liability, not conventional debt. cash_and_equivalents = 'Cash and Cash Equivalent' balance-sheet line only (1,866,634); there is also Rs.4,149,363k in 'Short Term Investments in Deposits' and a Rs.189,449k bank overdraft -- the cash flow statement's own 'Cash and Cash Equivalents at end of period' concept (5,826,549) nets deposits and overdraft together, but the balance-sheet line item is used here for a literal, citable figure. shares_in_issue = 165,488,271 voting + 24,201,719 non-voting = 189,689,990 (dual-class share structure; EPS is computed on this combined base per the filing's own Note 4). capex = Acquisition of PPE (204,578) + Acquisition of Biological Assets (2,985) = 207,563, which equals the period's entire 'Net Cash Used in Investing Activities' (207,563) since there was no other investing item (Construction of/Additions to Investment Property = nil this period). thesis.thesis_text: Renuka Holdings is the parent holding company of the Renuka group (including listed Agri Food Exports/Consumer Brands operations that consolidate results similar to those reported separately by Renuka Foods/COCO). Q1 FY2026/27 Group Revenue was roughly flat (-0.4% YoY to Rs.3,845.15mn), but Group Profit from Operations grew 58.8% YoY to Rs.338.88mn -- a genuine, segment-identified improvement, with the Agri Food Exports segment swinging from an Rs.8.97mn loss to an Rs.124.59mn profit (the same segment turnaround visible in Renuka Foods/COCO's own filing, corroborating the driver across both entities), while Consumer Brands segment profit fell 65.0% YoY. Below the operating line, a Fair Value Gain on FVTPL investments that had been Rs.306.29mn a year earlier collapsed to just Rs.14.37mn this quarter (-95.3%), partially offset by Finance Income rising 27x to Rs.293.27mn; net, Group PBT still grew 13.6% YoY to Rs.484.69mn. Critically, a first-time Rs.77.66mn tax charge (versus nil in the prior-year quarter) meant Group PAT actually FELL 4.6% YoY to Rs.407.04mn, and basic EPS fell 28.6% to Rs.0.78 as Non-Controlling Interest's profit share also grew. The parent company itself has no trading revenue and widened its standalone loss slightly (Rs.(1.575)mn vs Rs.(0.606)mn). The stock trades at a moderate discount to owners' book value (~0.75x P/B) and a reasonable ~14.5x annualized P/E given the operating-segment turnaround, but the PAT/EPS decline underneath the headline operating-profit growth is a real near-term earnings-quality caveat (interim filed 25-Aug-2026, source_doc_id 52652).
thesis.gaps_note: Macro & Industry Outlook (10% weight) unavailable -- renormalized across the remaining five pillars. Confidence is capped by having only one quarter of financials on file with no QoQ comparator (Q1 is the first quarter of RHL's FYE-March year). Genuine, unresolved filing-level gaps: (1) no qualitative explanation is given for the Agri Food Exports segment's swing from an Rs.8.97mn loss to an Rs.124.59mn profit, or for the Fair Value Gain on FVTPL investments collapsing from Rs.306.29mn to Rs.14.37mn; (2) COMPANY-basis segment detail is not disclosed at all; (3) two balance-sheet subtotal rows print their comparative-date columns in an apparently reversed order in the raw filing text, resolved here by re-summing component lines and cross-checking against the Operational Review narrative. RHL is the parent/related entity of a broader group that also includes BIL (covered separately in this database under a different agent's remit) -- noted here as context only; BIL's own data was not touched.

financial_quality.rationale: Strong liquidity (current ratio ~3.27x, current assets Rs.16,319.02mn / current liabilities Rs.4,994.83mn) and manageable leverage relative to owners' equity (~Rs.3,811.02mn borrowings vs Rs.9,972.68mn owners' equity, ~38%), but Group PAT actually fell 4.6% YoY (to Rs.407.04mn) despite a 13.6% PBT increase, due to a first-time Rs.77.66mn tax charge and a growing NCI profit share -- a real earnings-quality caveat beneath an otherwise solid balance sheet.

growth_outlook.rationale: Group Profit from Operations grew a genuine 58.8% YoY (to Rs.338.88mn), driven by a segment-identified Agri Food Exports turnaround (Rs.8.97mn loss to Rs.124.59mn profit) that is independently corroborated by the same segment's results at subsidiary Renuka Foods/COCO. However, Consumer Brands segment profit fell 65.0% YoY, and bottom-line Group PAT/EPS actually declined YoY, so growth at the operating-segment level has not yet translated into consolidated bottom-line growth.

valuation.rationale: At Rs.45.3/share (market cap Rs.7,496.62mn) against owners' equity of Rs.9,972.68mn, the stock trades at a moderate ~0.75x discount to book value and a reasonable ~14.5x annualized P/E given the operating-segment turnaround, though the PAT/EPS decline this quarter is a real near-term caveat on the earnings base used for that multiple.

business_quality.rationale: Diversified conglomerate parent across Agri Food Exports, Consumer Brands, and Investment segments, with meaningful scale (Rs.3,845.15mn quarterly Group revenue) but a complex NCI-heavy consolidated structure (NCI captured a growing share of profit this quarter) and a standalone parent entity with no trading revenue of its own (widening small parent-only loss to Rs.(1,575)k from Rs.(606)k).

governance_risk.rationale: No qualitative explanation is given anywhere in the filing for either the Agri Food Exports segment's swing from loss to profit or the 95.3% collapse in Fair Value Gain on FVTPL investments -- both large, unexplained non-operating/segment swings that this project treats as genuine, unresolved uncertainties rather than confirmed operating trends.

key_reasons: Group Profit from Operations grew 58.8% YoY to Rs.338.88mn, driven by a genuine, segment-identified turnaround in Agri Food Exports (Rs.8.97mn loss to Rs.124.59mn profit) that is independently corroborated by the same segment's results at subsidiary Renuka Foods/COCO
Strong balance-sheet liquidity (current ratio ~3.27x) and a moderate ~0.75x discount to owners' book value at a reasonable ~14.5x annualized P/E

Finance Income rose 27x YoY (Rs.10.76mn to Rs.293.27mn), partially offsetting a collapse in Fair Value Gains on FVTPL investments (Rs.306.29mn to Rs.14.37mn, -95.3%) and keeping Group PBT growth positive (+13.6%) despite that headwind
watch_factors: Group PAT actually FELL 4.6% YoY (to Rs.407.04mn) and basic EPS fell 28.6% (to Rs.0.78) despite the 58.8% operating-profit growth, because of a first-time Rs.77.66mn tax charge (nil PY) and a growing Non-Controlling Interest profit share -- the headline operating improvement does not flow through to the bottom line this quarter

Consumer Brands segment profit fell 65.0% YoY (Rs.83.13mn to Rs.29.11mn) even as Agri Food Exports turned around -- the two segments are moving in opposite directions and neither swing is explained by MD&A commentary in the filing

Fair Value Gain on FVTPL investments collapsed 95.3% YoY (Rs.306.29mn to Rs.14.37mn) with no explanation of which securities moved or why -- a large, unexplained non-operating swing that could reverse in either direction next quarter

horizon_notes.6m: Q2 FY2026/27 results will show whether the Agri Food Exports turnaround and Consumer Brands weakness both persist, and whether the tax-driven PAT/EPS decline was a one-off timing issue or a new steady-state effective tax rate.
horizon_notes.1y: If Agri Food Exports sustains its turnaround and Consumer Brands stabilises, Group PAT could recover to track the stronger operating-profit trend; continued FV-gain volatility or a widening NCI share would keep owners'-EPS growth subdued.
horizon_notes.3y: Thesis depends on the durability of the Agri Food Exports segment recovery (also visible at Renuka Foods/COCO) and on management's capital allocation across the group's diversified segments (Agri Food Exports, Consumer Brands, Investment).
horizon_notes.5y: No macro/industry data source in this project to assess Sri Lanka's multi-year agri-export demand and FX cycle relevant to the Agri Food Exports segment, or capital-market conditions relevant to the group's investment portfolio.

interim_updates.note_text: Renuka Holdings PLC (RHL) reported Group Revenue of Rs.3,845.15mn for Q1 FY2026/27 (quarter ended 30 June 2026), down marginally 0.4% YoY (2025: Rs.3,860.79mn), but Group Profit/(Loss) from Operations rose 58.8% YoY to Rs.338.88mn (2025: Rs.213.44mn) -- entirely a segment-mix story per the Segmental note (p.7): the Agri Food Exports segment swung from a Rs.8.97mn LOSS in Q1 FY2025/26 to a Rs.124.59mn PROFIT this quarter (a Rs.133.56mn positive swing, the single largest driver of the operating-profit improvement), while the Consumer Brands segment profit fell 65.0% YoY to Rs.29.11mn (2025: Rs.83.13mn). Below the operating line, the picture partly reverses: the Fair Value Gain on Investments measured at FVTPL collapsed 95.3% YoY to Rs.14.37mn from Rs.306.29mn (a Rs.291.92mn swing against the Investment segment, whose own segment profit fell 28.1% to Rs.253.34mn from Rs.352.52mn) -- confirmed via the PBT bridge (338.88mn operating + 131.44mn net finance income + 14.37mn FV gain = 484.69mn PBT, ties exactly) and corroborated by the raw PDF text, whose 'Fair Value Gain/(Loss)' row extracts with the two comparative years apparently reversed relative to the header order -- the 14,372/306,291 assignment used here was independently confirmed against the cash flow statement's identical adjustment line. Net Finance Income swung to a Rs.131.44mn INCOME from a Rs.93.05mn COST a year earlier (Finance Income rose 27x to Rs.293.27mn from Rs.10.76mn), which more than offset the FV-gain collapse and pushed Group PBT up 13.6% YoY to Rs.484.69mn (2025: Rs.426.68mn). Group Tax Expense of Rs.77.66mn was levied this quarter versus NIL tax in the 30.06.2025 comparator (which is why PAT2025=PBT2025 exactly, Rs.426.68mn), so Group PAT actually FELL 4.6% YoY to Rs.407.04mn despite the 13.6% PBT growth -- the swing from a zero-tax to a taxed quarter is the specific driver of PAT underperforming PBT. Basic EPS fell to Rs.0.78 from Rs.1.09 (-28.6%), a steeper decline than PAT because Non-Controlling Interest's share of profit rose to Rs.259.44mn from Rs.219.39mn, shrinking the portion attributable to Equity Holders of the Parent to Rs.147.60mn from Rs.207.29mn (-28.8%), which is what EPS is computed on. At Company (parent, standalone holding-company) level, RHL has no trading revenue; PBT was a Rs.1.575mn LOSS vs a smaller Rs.0.606mn LOSS a year earlier, driven purely by Administrative Expenses of Rs.1.776mn (2025: Rs.0.790mn) with no offsetting dividend income this quarter -- immaterial in scale but worth noting the loss widened.
interim_updates.gaps_note: No QoQ comparison possible: this is RHL's first financial_statements/interim_updates entry in this DB for FY2026/27 (Q1 is the first quarter of RHL's FYE-March fiscal year, so there is no prior-quarter-within-this-DB to compare against; only the YoY comparator column printed in the filing itself is used). Genuine filing-level gaps: (1) no qualitative MD&A explains WHY the Agri Food Exports segment swung from a Rs.8.97mn loss to a Rs.124.59mn profit -- the segmental note gives the number but not the driver (export volume, pricing, or FX pass-through); (2) similarly no explanation is given for the Fair Value Gain on FVTPL investments collapsing from Rs.306.29mn to Rs.14.37mn (which securities, what moved); (3) two balance-sheet subtotal rows ('Total Non-Current Assets', 'Total Current Liabilities') print their two comparative-date columns in reversed order in the raw PDF text relative to the header and their own component lines -- resolved here by re-summing each subtotal's own component lines rather than trusting the printed subtotal's column position, and cross-checked against the Operational Review text on p.2, which independently states Total Current Assets of Rs.16,319mn; (4) COMPANY-basis segment detail is not disclosed at all (segmental note is Group-only).
interim_updates.takeaway: RHL's headline Group operating-profit growth of 58.8% YoY is a genuine, segment-identifiable improvement concentrated in Agri Food Exports (Rs.8.97mn loss to Rs.124.59mn profit), while Consumer Brands weakened materially (-65.0%). Below the operating line, the story is more mixed: a large Fair Value Gain on FVTPL investments booked in Q1 FY2025/26 (Rs.306.29mn) did not repeat at anything like the same scale this quarter (Rs.14.37mn only), and a first-time Rs.77.66mn tax charge (versus nil last year) meant Group PAT actually declined 4.6% YoY and EPS fell 28.6% to Rs.0.78, despite the operating and PBT-level improvement. Investors reading only the PBT/operating-profit growth figures would miss that bottom-line PAT and EPS both moved in the opposite direction, driven by the tax swing and a shrinking parent-attributable profit share as NCI's portion grew.
operational_highlights: Group Revenue Rs.3,845.15mn, -0.4% YoY (2025: Rs.3,860.79mn); Group Profit from Operations Rs.338.88mn, +58.8% YoY; Group PBT Rs.484.69mn, +13.6% YoY; Group PAT Rs.407.04mn, -4.6% YoY (2025: Rs.426.68mn).

Agri Food Exports segment swung from a Rs.8.97mn LOSS to a Rs.124.59mn PROFIT YoY (Rs.133.56mn swing) -- the largest single driver of the 58.8% operating-profit growth; Consumer Brands segment profit fell 65.0% YoY to Rs.29.11mn (2025: Rs.83.13mn).
Fair Value Gain on FVTPL Investments collapsed 95.3% YoY to Rs.14.37mn (2025: Rs.306.29mn), dragging the Investment segment's own profit down 28.1% to Rs.253.34mn.

Finance Income rose to Rs.293.27mn from Rs.10.76mn PY (27x), swinging Net Finance Income/(Cost) to a Rs.131.44mn INCOME from a Rs.93.05mn COST -- more than offset the FV-gain collapse at the PBT line.
Group Tax Expense of Rs.77.66mn was charged this quarter vs NIL in 30.06.2025 -- the specific reason PAT fell 4.6% YoY despite PBT growing 13.6%.

Basic EPS fell to Rs.0.78 from Rs.1.09 (-28.6%), steeper than the PAT decline because Non-Controlling Interest's profit share rose to Rs.259.44mn from Rs.219.39mn, shrinking parent-attributable profit to Rs.147.60mn from Rs.207.29mn.

Company (parent, standalone) PBT loss widened to Rs.(1.575)mn from Rs.(0.606)mn PY, driven by Administrative Expenses of Rs.1.776mn (2025: Rs.0.790mn) with no trading revenue or offsetting dividend income.
key_drivers: Agri Food Exports segment turnaround (Rs.8.97mn loss to Rs.124.59mn profit, a Rs.133.56mn swing) is the dominant driver of the 58.8% Group operating-profit growth.
A swing from zero tax (30.06.2025) to a Rs.77.66mn tax charge (30.06.2026) is the specific reason Group PAT fell 4.6% YoY even as PBT rose 13.6%.
Fair Value Gain on FVTPL investments collapsing from Rs.306.29mn to Rs.14.37mn (-95.3%) is a material drag partially offset by a 27x rise in Finance Income (Rs.10.76mn to Rs.293.27mn).

_gaps: ebitda: depreciation_amortization not disclosed; EBITDA understated (= operating profit only)
